report: # 1. Executive Diagnosis + Summary of Reason IIMK_PCPF_10 delivered **mixed performance**: it materially exceeded volume and GSV plans, but applications, enrollments, conversion rates, and observed-spend efficiency declined versus both prior batches. The higher ₹240,000 fee supported GSV plan attainment, although Actual GSV remained below historical batches. - Actual GSV reached **₹12.48M**, **₹4.43M above plan** and at **155.0% attainment**. - Leads, applications, and enrollments exceeded plan by **73.5%**, **60.0%**, and **48.6%**, respectively. - Observed spend was **₹2.73M**, **46.3% above** the ₹1.87M planned budget. - Versus IIMK_PCPF_09, applications fell **27.3%** and enrollments fell **27.8%**, despite leads declining only **7.5%**. - The historical funnel gap was concentrated before application: L2W declined **0.7 pp** and W2A declined **1.2 pp** versus IIMK_PCPF_09; A2E was comparatively stable at **81.3%**. - Observed-spend CPL and CAC increased **19.7%** and **53.3%**, respectively, versus IIMK_PCPF_09. # 2. Actual GSV is calculated as 52 enrollments × the program-level fee of ₹240,000.* The most material plan gap was observed spend, which exceeded planned budget by **₹863,264**, or **46.3%**. Nevertheless, enrollments and Actual GSV also exceeded plan, with GSV finishing **₹4.43M above target**. # 3. Current vs previous batch ## 3.1 Volume and commercial outcomes | Metric | IIMK_PCPF_10 | IIMK_PCPF_09 | Change vs PCPF_09 | IIMK_PCPF_08 | Change vs PCPF_08 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Leads | 4,260 | 4,604 | ↓ 7.5% | 5,313 | ↓ 19.8% | | Warm leads | 1,354 | 1,496 | ↓ 9.5% | 1,484 | ↓ 8.8% | | Applications | 64 | 88 | ↓ 27.3% | 86 | ↓ 25.6% | | Enrollments | 52 | 72 | ↓ 27.8% | 76 | ↓ 31.6% | | Program fee | ₹240,000 | ₹210,000 | +14.3% | ₹210,000 | +14.3% | | Actual GSV | ₹12,480,000 | ₹15,120,000 | ↓ 17.5% | ₹15,960,000 | ↓ 21.8% | The higher program fee partially offset lower enrollment volume, but Actual GSV remained **17.5% below IIMK_PCPF_09** and **21.8% below IIMK_PCPF_08**. ## 3.2 Conversion and acquisition efficiency | Metric | IIMK_PCPF_10 | IIMK_PCPF_09 | Change vs PCPF_09 | IIMK_PCPF_08 | Change vs PCPF_08 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | L2W | 31.8% | 32.5% | ↓ 0.7 pp | 27.9% | ↑ 3.9 pp | | L2A | 1.5% | 1.9% | ↓ 0.4 pp | 1.6% | ↓ 0.1 pp | | L2E | 1.2% | 1.6% | ↓ 0.3 pp | 1.4% | ↓ 0.2 pp | | W2A | 4.7% | 5.9% | ↓ 1.2 pp | 5.8% | ↓ 1.1 pp | | A2E | 81.3% | 81.8% | ↓ 0.6 pp | 88.4% | ↓ 7.1 pp | | CPL | ₹641 | ₹535 | ↑ 19.7% | ₹481 | ↑ 33.2% | | CAC | ₹52,486 | ₹34,234 | ↑ 53.3% | ₹33,623 | ↑ 56.1% | CPL and CAC are based on observed spend. Versus IIMK_PCPF_09, the larger funnel deterioration occurred in W2A rather than A2E: applications per warm lead declined **1.2 pp**, while application-to-enrollment conversion declined only **0.6 pp**. # 4. Source-wise root-cause analysis **Observation:** Overall lead volume exceeded plan, so insufficient lead generation was not the plan-level constraint; however, historical L2A weakened. Facebook generated the most leads but had low L2W and W2A, while Google produced the most applications and enrollments. **Observation:** Website recorded the highest L2E among sources with meaningful enrollment output, but on only 72 leads; referral had higher rates on just 13 leads and is therefore not adequate for a scale conclusion. **Hypothesis:** The concentration of 2,158 leads in Facebook alongside low warm-lead and application conversion may have diluted aggregate funnel performance, but the evidence does not establish the underlying cause. **Coverage limitation:** Source-level spend is available only for Google, LinkedIn, and Facebook; CPL and CAC comparisons are therefore observed-spend metrics, and unpaid or unreported source economics are N/A. | Source | Leads | Warm leads | Applications | Enrollments | L2W | L2A | L2E | W2A | A2E | Observed spend | CPL | CAC | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Google | 640 | 184 | 20 | 15 | 28.8% | 3.1% | 2.3% | 10.9% | 75.0% | ₹1,445,985 | ₹2,259 | ₹96,399 | | Database | 520 | 478 | 11 | 9 | 91.9% | 2.1% | 1.7% | 2.3% | 81.8% | N/A | N/A | N/A | | Website | 72 | 38 | 9 | 9 | 52.8% | 12.5% | 12.5% | 23.7% | 100.0% | N/A | N/A | N/A | | Others | 155 | 89 | 8 | 7 | 57.4% | 5.2% | 4.5% | 9.0% | 87.5% | N/A | N/A | N/A | | LinkedIn | 676 | 170 | 6 | 6 | 25.1% | 0.9% | 0.9% | 3.5% | 100.0% | ₹447,258 | ₹662 | ₹74,543 | | Referral | 13 | 13 | 3 | 3 | 100.0% | 23.1% | 23.1% | 23.1% | 100.0% | N/A | N/A | N/A | | Facebook | 2,158 | 370 | 6 | 2 | 17.1% | 0.3% | 0.1% | 1.6% | 33.3% | ₹836,021 | ₹387 | ₹418,011 | | Affiliate | 26 | 12 | 1 | 1 | 46.2% | 3.8% | 3.8% | 8.3% | 100.0% | N/A | N/A | N/A | # 5. Advisor-tenure mix The equal-weight priority score is calculated as **(L2W + L2E) / 2**. The **00–03 month** group ranked highest at 29.4%, supported by 756 leads, while the **24+ month** group ranked lowest at 11.3% across 714 leads; these are associations and do not establish that tenure caused the performance difference. | Rank | Advisor tenure | Leads | Warm leads | Applications | Enrollments | L2W | L2E | Equal-weight score | |---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 00 to 03 | 756 | 436 | 11 | 8 | 57.7% | 1.1% | 29.4% | | 2 | NA / missing | 178 | 96 | 5 | 4 | 53.9% | 2.2% | 28.1% | | 3 | 13 to 24 | 588 | 176 | 15 | 15 | 29.9% | 2.6% | 16.2% | | 4 | 07 to 12 | 1,712 | 421 | 24 | 17 | 24.6% | 1.0% | 12.8% | | 5 | 04 to 06 | 312 | 70 | 2 | 2 | 22.4% | 0.6% | 11.5% | | 6 | 24+ | 714 | 156 | 7 | 6 | 21.8% | 0.8% | 11.3% | The 07–12 month group handled the largest lead volume—**1,712 leads**—but ranked fourth on the score. The 24+ month group’s bottom ranking and the 00–03 month group’s top ranking warrant workflow and allocation review, but the available data cannot isolate advisor capability from source mix or lead quality. # 6. Prioritized actions 1. **Address the warm-lead-to-application gap.** Review follow-up, qualification, and application-start records because W2A declined to **4.7%**, down **1.2 pp** versus IIMK_PCPF_09 and **1.1 pp** versus IIMK_PCPF_08. 2. **Reassess Facebook scale before further allocation.** Facebook supplied **50.7% of leads** but only 2 enrollments, with **0.1% L2E** and an observed-spend CAC of **₹418,011**; Marketing should validate targeting, lead validity, and campaign-level conversion records before changing spend. 3. **Protect and test higher-converting source opportunities.** Examine whether website and referral performance can be replicated at greater volume, while recognizing their limited bases of 72 and 13 leads, respectively. 4. **Validate spend and attribution coverage.** Finance and Marketing should reconcile the **₹2.73M observed spend** against the ₹1.87M budget and confirm whether missing source-level spend reflects unpaid channels, incomplete attribution, or unreported costs; the current evidence cannot determine the cause. 5. **Audit advisor/source allocation.** Compare source mix, lead age, and follow-up activity across tenure groups—especially 00–03, 07–12, and 24+ months—before attributing score differences to tenure or making staffing decisions.
